2: This ordinance shall apply to all mining operations and data centers installed, constructed, or modified after the effective date of this Ordinance. Mining operations or data centers in place before the effective date of this ordinance shall not be required to meet the requirements of this ordinance unless abandonment, closure, replacement, alteration, or expansion ofoperation thereon is enacted. All mining operations and data centers shall be designed, erected, and installed following all applicable Local, State, and Federal codes, regulations, and standards.

4.1 Abandonntent/Removal of Facilities. Any mining operation or data center that is not operated for a continuous period of twelve (12) months and for which there are no applications pending for permitted use of the structure at the end of such twelve-month period, shall be considered abandoned, whether or not the owner or operator intends to make use of the device(s). The owner of an abandoned server farm, mining operation, or data center, and the owner of the properry where such is located shall be under a duty to remove facilities, components, and equipment relating to operations of the facilities. If such facilities are not removed within a reasonable time, not to exceed ninety (90) consecutive days, after receipt of notice from the governing authority notiffing the owner(s) of such abandonment, the governing authority may remove such facilities and place a lien upon the property for the costs of removal. The goveming authority may pursue all legal remedies available to it to insure that abandoned component(s) are removed. Delay by the governing authority in taking action shall not in any way waive the governing authority's right to take action. Airport Regulations. No mining operations or data center may be installed within 1 nautical miles of an airport or helipad without the approval of an airport or helipad's appropriate authority before construction. 4.3 4.4 4.5 4.6 4.7 4.8 4.9 4.10 4.11 Building Permits and Structural Safety. All applicable building permits must be obtained prior to tlre construction of a mining operation or data center. Building Placenrcnt. All mining operations and data centers must adhere to the following building placement requirements: (i) Minimum lot frontage: One hundred ten (l l0) feet adjoining a road. (ii) Minimum lot width at building line: One hundred ten (l l0) feet. (iii) Minimum lot acreage: Ten (10) acres. Design Contpliance. The design of a mining operation or data center must conform to applicable local, state, and national standards, and to all local regulations. All design and installation work must comply with the National Electric Code (NEC), the International Residential Code (lRC), the International Commercial Building Code, the State Fire Code, and any additional requirements set by the local utility for grid-connected systems or by the Toombs County Code Enforcement Department. Electrical Connections. All electrical interconnection and distribution lines within a mining operation or data center's boundaries, except for power lines that leave the project or are within a substation, shall be underground, unless Toombs County Code Enforcement Department grants a written exception due to severe environmental constraints. Emergency Response Plan. Mining operations and data centers shall have a written emergency response plan that shall be approved by the Toombs County Code Enforcement Department, sherifPs office, fire department, and emergency management agency. Each operation shall update its emergency response ptan no later than January I of each year with a copy provided to all departments and agenciei named in this subsection. The emergency response plan shall include the following: (i) Phone number, email address, and street address for all manufacturers, installers, owners, and operators; and (ii) Phone number, email address, and mailing address for a representative of the operation responsible for responding to public inquiries; and (iii) Material safety data sheets that apply to any materials of the operation's facility; and (iv) Clearly marked means and instructions for shutting down the operation. Equipment Space. Any equipment used in a mining operation or data center shall be housed in a rnit".ed, eleitrically grounded, and pre-engineered metal-encased structure with a fire rating designed to resist an internal electrical fire for at least 30 minutes. The containment space shall contain baffles that will automatically close in the event of fire independent of a possible electric system failure. Fencing.The perimeter of mining operations and data centers, including any visual buffer, shall be enclosed by a black or green vinyl coated-chain link fence with a height of at least six feet, a gate, and locking mechanism to deny access to any individuals not authorized to be on the property and for public safety. All mining operations shall have a knox box entry system at the primary entrance, which shall comply with the specifications of the International Fire Code. Ground Water Testing. A minimum of at least one twenty (20) foot ground monitoring well shall be installed for each mining operation or data center as determined by the Toombs County Code Enforcement Department. The required well shall be tested for the presence of any heavy metals or regulated contaminants. After initial testing, a biannual test shall be required for two consecutive years. If no heavy metals or contaminants are identified in the first two testing periods, each a period consisting of one (1) year, testing may shift to a five (5) year schedule. The well shall also be tested prior to any decommissioning. Alltest results shall be submitted to the Toombs County Code Enforcement Department. Lighting. Exterior lighting shall be designed and constructed with fully shielded fixtures that direct light downward and into the interior of the property and away from adjacent roads and adjacent properties. Noise. Mining operations and data centers must adhere to the noise standards to avoid contribution to excessive noise pollution. The following noise limits shall apply: 4.12
4: - (i) During daytime hours (8:00 AM to 7:59 PM), the continuous sound level generated by the mining operation or data center shall not exceed 50 decibels, measured at a distance of 25 feet from the property line of the mining operation. (ii) During nighttime hours (8:00 PM to 7:59 AM), the continuous sound level generated by the mining operation or data center shall not exceed 35 decibels, measured at a distance of 25 feet from the property line of the mining operation. An initial noise level study must be completed before construction begins to establish a baseline decibel level, for both DbA and DbC, at all adjoining property lines. DbA is audible noise and DbC measures specific frequencies and can measure tonal/narrow band low-frequency humming. After the completion of the construction and before a certificate of occupancy and/or business license can be issued, a follow-up noise study must be completed at all adjacent property lines. There can be no increase in the noise level from the preconstruction baseline at the property lines of all adjoining properties. 4.13 Ownership and Maintenance. Unless otherwise specified in a contract or agreement, the property owner of record will be presumed responsible for owning and maintaining the mining operations or data center on their property, and they will also be responsible for removal of facilities, components, and equipment of the operation unless specified otherwise. 4.14 Pollution Restrictions. Any use or activity producing air, dust, smoke, glare, exhaust, heat, or humidity in any form shall be carried on in such a manner that it is not perceptible at or beyond the property line. 4.15 Setbacks. Mining operations and data center buildings shall have a setback of at least five hundred (500) feet from the propefty line. 4.16 Signage. Brightly colored signs, no smaller than one foot by two feet, shall be posted on the p"iirnit". fence of mining operation and data center. These signs shall be placed at intervals of every 100 feet and must include the following information: (i) Owner/Operator ldentification: Name(s) and phone number(s) of the owner, operator, and installer of the mining operations or data center; and (ii) Emergency Contact Information: A 24-hour emergency contact phone number. All signage shall comply with applicable State, Federal, and county requirements for displaying advertisements or signage. The signs shall be maintained in good condition for the lifetime of the mining operation or data center. The responsibility for maintaining the signage lies with the owner or operator of the facilities. Signs containing educational information about Cryptocurrency, Data Mining, Mining Operations, and Data Centers may also be posted, provided they do not interfere with the primary waming and informational signage req uirements. 4.17 Solar Energt Systents. When ground mounted on the premises of mining operations and data centers, solar energy systems shall be screened with a minimum structural buffer of twenty (20) feet meeting the requirements of Sections 4.1 5 and 4.20. If roof mounted, the solar energy system shall be screened to not be visible from any adjoining road or adjoining property. 4.1 8 Structure Requiremenls. All principal and accessory structures used for mining operations and data centers shall be arranged, designed, and constructed to be harmonious and compatible with the site and with the surrounding properties in a manner that reduces its unsightly view from residential dwelling units and/or roadways. The followed standards are also required: (i) All structures shall have concrete foundations; (ii) All exterior walls visible from any public right-of-way, the building fagade viewable from the right-of-way shall incorporate at least two of the following design features to break up the building mass: i. Vertical or horizontal articulation of the fagade at intervals not exceeding 50 feet. ii. Variation in building height of at least l0olo across the fagade, or stepped rooflines. iii. Use of architecturalprojections or recesses at least 2 feet in depth. iv. Changes in fagade materials or colors with a minimum of two types of materials. (iii) If the building is visible from any public right-of-way, the elevation of that wall shall contain fenestration of at least 30% of the gross wall area measured above grade; (iv) No structure shall be defective, decayed or corroded; (v) Shipping containers shall not be used as a structure for mining operations; and (vi) All exterior facades that do not face a public roadway or residential area shall comply with subsections (ii) and (iii), above, or may have muted earth tone colors.

Mining operations and data centers shall provide a maximum of two (2) parking spaces for each employee assigned to the facility, based on the maximum number of employees on-site at any one time. All roadways, driveways, and parking areas on a mining operation or data center premises shall be curbed and guttered for appropriate drainage. Utility Grid Connection. Mining operations and data centers may not be connected to any electric utility grid without prior approval from the applicable electric utility entity. Prior to operation, all electrical connections must be inspected by an authorized electrical inspector/agency and approved by the Toombs County Code Enforcement Department. Prior to approval by the Toombs County Code Enforcement Department, the applicant shall provide written verification from the electrical service provider stating the following: (i) Adequate capacity is available on the applicable supply lines and substation to ensure that the capacity available to serve the other needs of the service area is consistent with the normal projected load growth envisioned by the provider; (ii) Utility supply equipment and related electrical infrastructure are sufficiently sized and can safely accommodate the proposed use; (iii) The use will not cause electrical interference or fluctuations in line voltage on and off the operating premises; and (iv) Written verification that the electrical work has passed the third-party's final inspection. Vegetation Maintenance. Clearing of natural vegetation shall be limited to that which is necessary foi the construction, operation, and maintenance of the mining operation or data center and consistent with best practices forthe preservation ofnatural areas or good husbandry ofthe land or forest. Except for the visual buffer and the areas not cleared for construction or returned to natural vegetation by replanting of trees, the height of any vegetation within a mining operation or data ".nt"r shall not exceed twelve inches and shall be no less than two inches in height over the soil surface. Visual Buffer. Except for areas of ingress and egress into the site of a mining operation or data center, ali mechanical equipment, structures, and components of operations shall have, to the extent reasonably practicable, a visual buffer of natural vegetation and/or plantings to provide a reasonable visual screen to reduce the unsightly view of the mining operation or data center. (i) The visual buffer shall consist of shrubbery, trees, and/or other non-invasive plant species which provide a screen with a mature height of at least six (6) feet above the tallest structure or component. (ii) The viiual buffer should continue no less than one hundred (100) feet from any federal or state highway and fifty (50) feet from any county roadway. (iii) The visual buffer shall be maintained for the life of the mining operation or data center at the responsibility of the owner or operator of the mining operation. (iv) The viiual buffer shall provide at least seventy-five percent (75%) screening of the mining operation or data center. Waivers. The Toombs County Code Enforcement Department may not waive any of the above￾listed conditions and may add additional conditions or safeguards as needed for public health, safety, and welfare or to mitigate the impact of the facility on surrounding properties and uses. Violations of any such additionalconditions or safeguards shall be a violation of this Ordinance. Waste. All waste generated by mining operations and data centers must be disposed of in accordance with applicable state, federal, and local laws and regulations. Electronic waste, including discarded etectronic devices and components (i.e., computers, servers, and other hardware) must be disposed of through approved recycling or disposal methods. Additionally, mining operations and data centers must maintain records of e-waste disposal, including the quantity of e-waste disposed of, the method of disposal, and the disposal or recycling facility used. ih"r" records must be made available to Toombs County Code Enforcement Department and other applicable regulatory authorities upon request. Water Consumption and Cooling Systems. Mining operations and data centers shall incorporate performance .iasu.es designed to limit potable water consumption, including the use of closed￾loop or similar systems designed to minimize consumption and eliminate continuous discharge or evaporative loss. An applicant shall disclose daily water consumption and usage on their initial application. If actual usage increases by more than l0% from the amount initially disclosed, the applicant's pennit shall be forfeited, and the applicant must submit a new permit application.

Before commencing the operation of any Commercial Cryptocurrency, Data Mining, andlor Data Center, the owner(s) or operator(s) of any such operations shall submit an application for a mining or data center permit on the form prescribed by the Toombs County Code Enforcement Department and shall provide proof of compliance with all the respective standards outlined in this Ordinance. The "Toombs County Cryptocurrency and Data Center Permit Application" must include the following components: (i) Basic Information: The applicant shall provide a document that includes: (a) The address of the property where the operation will be located. (b) The applicant's name, address, telephone number, and email address. (c) The property owner's name, address, telephone number, and email address. (d) The operator's name, address, telephone number, and email address. (e) Evidence ofthe applicant's control ofthe property, such as a deed, lease, or option agreement with the landowner. (ii) Comprehensive Site Plan: The applicant shall submit the following based on the most current and accurate information available: (a) A site plan depicting the locations of all existing and proposed structures, including, inverters, transformers, water tanks, cooling systems, grading, substations, lighting, computers, landscape plans, buildings, property lines, rights￾of-way, roads, required setbacks, and visual buffers. (b) A visual buffer plan that demonstrates compliance with the following: ( I ) Minimizing impacts on adjacent properties as required by this ordinance. (2) Preserving natural tree growth and landforms along the perimeter of the property as required by this ordinance. (3) Adhering to additional visual buffer requirements set forth in this Ordinance. (c) A list identifuing (a) federal or state endangered, threatened, or candidate species that may be present on the property or within 1,000 feet and (b) critical habitat on the property or within 1,000 feet. (d) A plan for removal of the mining operation that includes: (l) Name, address, phone number, and email address for the responsible person(s) or entity; (2) Detailing of the structures, components, and non-utility owned equipment to be removed. (3) A plan for recycling or reusing materials to the extent practicable. (4) A restoration plan to return the property to a condition suitable for the designated land use. (5) A timeline for completing the removal that meets the requirements set forth in Section 4.1 of this Ordinance. (iii) Certifications: The applicant shall submit an affidavit affirming: (a) The construction and operation of the Commercial Cryptocurrency, Data Mining, and/or Data Center facility will comply with all applicable federal and state laws. (b) The construction and operation of the Commercial Cryptocurrency, Data Mining, and/or Data Center facility will comply with all local laws, including this Ordinance. Inspection.No property owner or facility operator shall commence construction or operations until it has been inspected by the Toombs County Code Enforcement Department and obtained the permit required by this section. Review of Apptication. Upon receiving a Toombs County Cryptocurrency and Data Center Permit Application, the Toombs County Code Enforcement Department shall conduct permitting proceedings. An application may be denied if it is determined the mining operation or data center does not comply with local requirements. In reviewing an application, the Toombs County Code Enforcement Department shall consider various criteria, including but not limited to the following: (i) the effect of the proposed activity on traffic flow along adjoining streets; (ii) the amount and location of open space; (iii) the adequacy ofscreening to protect adjacent property from any negative impacts; (iv) the provision of ingress and egress to the property; (v) the compatibility of the proposed use with adjacent uses and any negative impacts; (vi) whether the proposed use is consistent with the Comprehensive Plan; and (vii) any other factors necessary to provide adequate protection for the health, safety, and welfare of Toombs County citizens. 5.2 5.3

The Comprehensive Site PIan must be approved in writing by the Toombs County Code Enforcement Departrnent before an applicant may receive a permit or commence operations. Permit Fee. Atthe time of application, each applicant shall pay a non-refundable permit fee of two thousand five-hundred dollars ($2,500) to the Toombs County Code Enforcement Department. Decommissioning Plan. The owner or developer of a data center must submit a decommissioning plan to the Toombs County Code Enforcement Department prior to the issuance of a building permit for a data center. (i) Plan Contents: Tlre decommissioning plan shall include, at a minimum: (a) Timeline: A detailed timeline for the decommissioning process, including key milestones and estimated completion dates for each phase of the decommissioning activities. (b) Equipment and Material Removal Procedures: Specific procedures for the safe dismantling and removal of all equipment, materials, and structures from the data center site. This should include methods for handling and transporting equipment to prevent damage and ensure safety. (c) Hazardous Materials: Detailed methods for identifuing, handling, and disposal of hazardous materials in compliance with federal, state and local regulations. This should include a list of all hazardous materials present on-site and procedures for their safe removal and disposal. (d) Site Remediation Plan: A comprehensrve plan for site remediation including Soil and ground water testing, identification of contaminants, and proposed clean up measures. This should include a timeline for remediation activities and methods for monitoring and verifuing the effectiveness of the remediation efforts. (ii) Decommissioning Compliance: (a) Compliance during the decommissioning process will be monitored through several key methods to ensure that all activities adhere to the approved decommissioning plan and applicable regulations. Here are the primary methods: ( I ) Regular Inspections: The Toombs County Code Enforcement Department will conduct regular inspections of the data center site. These inspections will verifr that the decommissioning activities are being carried out according to the approved plan and identifu any deviations or non￾compliance issues early in the process. (2) Progress Reports: Developers are required to submit quarterly reports to the Toombs County Code Enforcement Department detailing the decommissioning activities completed during the reporting period. These reports will include summaries of work done, any deviations, and updated timelines for the remaining activities. This ensures continuous oversight and accountability. (3) Final Report: Upon completion of the decommissioning process, developers must submit to the Toombs County Code Enforcement Department a comprehensive final report. This report will include a detailed account of all decommissioning activities, documentation of equipment and hazardous materials removed, evidence of site remediation and restoration, compliance certificate, financial summary, and a community impact assessment, (4) Documentation and Record Keeping: Maintaining thorough documentation and records of all decommissioning activities is crucial. This includes records ofequipment removal, hazardous materials disposal, site remediation efforts, and compliance with data protection regulations. Proper documentation ensures tran sparency and traceabi lity. (5) Third-party Audits: In some cases, third-party audits may be conducted to provide an independent assessment of the decommissioning process. These audits can help verifu compliance with regulations and industry standards, ensuring that all activities are performed responsibly and safely. Decommissioning Bond. Developers must provide a decommissioning bond to cover the cost of decommissioning, removal, remediation, and mitigation of the property. The bond amount shall be adequate to ensure the complete decommissioning of the data center and restoration of the site. (i) Bond Amount Determination: The amount of the decommissioning bond shall be detennined by the Toombs County Board of Commissioners based on an estimate provided by a qualified independent engineer. The estimate shall include: (a) Costs for the removal of all equipment and materials. i 5.7

- (b) Costs for the disposal of hazardous materials. (c) Costs for site remediation and mitigation, including soil and groundwater testing and cleanup if necessary. (d) Costs for site restoration, including re-vegetation and any necessary landscaping. (ii) Bond Review and Adjustment: The bond amount shall be reviewed and adjusted periodically, as determined by the Toombs County Board of Commissioners, to ensure it remains adequate to cover 125Yo of the decommissioning costs. (iii) Form of Financial Assurance: Financial assurance may be provided in the form of a bond, escrow account, letter of credit, or other financial instrument acceptable to the Toombs County Board of Commissioners. The form of financial assurance must be sufficient to cover the estimated costs of decommissioning, removal, remediation, and restoration. (iv) Release of Financial Assurance: Financial assuiance shall not be released until the Toombs County Code Enforcement Department has verified that the decommissioning, removal, remediation, and site restoration have been completed in accordance with the approved decommissioning plan and all applicable regulations. A final inspection and approval by the Toombs County Code Enforcement Department is required before the release of the financial assurance. (v) Use of Financial Assurance: If the developer fails to complete the decommissioning, removal, remediation and site restoration as required, the Toombs County Board of Commissioners shall have the right to use the financial assurance to cover the cost of completing the decommissioning process. Any remaining funds after the completion of the decommissioning process shall be returned to the developer. (vi) Reporting Requirements: (a) Progress Reports: Developers must submit quarterly progress reports to the Toombs County Code Enforcement Department during the decommissioning process. These reports shall include: (l ) A summary of decommissioning activities completed during the reporting period. (2) Any deviations from the approved decommissioning plan and the reason for such deviations. (3) An update timeline for the remaining decommissioning activities. (vii) Final Report: Upon completion of the decommissioning process, developers must submit a final report to the Toombs County Code Enforcement Department. The final report shall include: (a) Detailed Account of Decommissioning Activities: A comprehensive description of all decommissioning activities performed, including the dismantling and removal of equipment, structures, and materials. (b) Documentation of Removal and Disposal: Records and receipts documenting the removal and proper disposal of all equipment, materials, and hazardous substances in accordance with federal, state and local regulations. (c) Site Remediation and Restoration Evidence: Evidence of site remediation and restoration efforts, including soil and groundwater testing results, photographs of the site before and after decommissioning, and any necessary environmental cleanup reports. (d) Compliance Certification: A statement certifuing that the decommissioning was completed in accordance with the approved decommissioning plan and all applicable regulations. This certification should be signed by a qualified independent engineer or environmental consultant. (e) Financial Summary: A financial summary detailing the costs incurred during the decommissioning process, including the use of decommissioning bond funds. (f) Community Impact Assessment: An assessment of the impact of the decommissioning on the surrounding community, including any measure taken to mitigate negative effects and feedback from community stakeholders. This assessment should include: (l) Community Engagement: Documentation of any community meetings or consultations held during the decommissioning process, including feedback received and how it was addressed. (2) Mitigation Measures: Details of any measures taken to mitigate negative impacts on the community, such as noise reduction, traffic management, and dust control. (3) Post-Decommissioning Use: Information on the intended future use of the site and any plans for redevelopment or repurpose. Reyocation of Permit.
